title: ASHG 2026 Featured Symposia
bodyHtml:
If you’re attending American Society of Human Genetics (ASHG) 2026, we invite you to join us for our Featured Symposia exploring how artificial intelligence and knowledge graphs are creating new opportunities for human genetics research and biomedical discovery.

Integrating AI and Knowledge Graphs for Human Genetics and Beyond: Innovations from the NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem

? Wednesday, October 21, 2026
⏰ 8:15–9:45 AM
? Convention Center, Room 710A / Level 7
? CEU Credits: 1.50
?‍? Add to show planner

This session introduces open-access resources for human genetics developed within the NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE), an initiative that promotes reuse and integration of data and resources generated by NIH Common Fund programs. Speakers will describe a series of CFDE resources that leverage artificial intelligence (AI) and knowledge graphs to promote data integration from disparate programs, including AI-ready cellular maps, protein-centric annotations, harmonized knowledge graphs, and LLM-assisted genomic exploration tools. The session will show how CFDE resources support integrative and reproducible analyses, and how AI and knowledge graphs can be leveraged more broadly for discovery within human genetics and biomedicine.

Moderators: Noël Burtt and Lucas Gillenwater
Speakers: Jake Chen, Cathy Wu, Deanne Taylor, and Chase Yakaboski

Whether you work in human genetics, genomics, data science, AI, or biomedical informatics, we hope you’ll join us to discover new resources, approaches, and opportunities for connecting data across the biomedical research ecosystem.
summary: Integrating AI and Knowledge Graphs for Human Genetics and Beyond: Innovations from the NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem
